Q: Everton’s Thierno Barry seems to be bringing back iconic dance moves after every goal.
VERDICT: BUY THIERNO BARRY Another in-form player, Thierno Barry (£5.7m) is fourth among forwards for points (55), with six goals and one assist in 10 matches.

Barry has notched 13 goal involvements (10 goals, three assists) in all competitions so far this season, most recently a quick-fire brace in the Blues' 3-1 come-from-behind victory over Coventry City prior to the international break.

After three goals, an assist and 25 points over the latest two Fantasy Premier League (FPL) Gameweeks, Everton’s Thierno Barry (£5.7m) is currently the second most-bought player of this international break.

Barry’s goals took him to double figures across all competitions for the campaign, with only Erling Haaland (nine) and Alexander Isak (seven) having struck more Premier League goals this season than Barry (six).
Asked about his strong form, Barry told evertontv : “I'm very happy because it's always a pleasure to score and I'm so happy to do my first assist in the Premier League.
BARRY FRONT AND CENTRE Above: Everton players sorted by shots and big chances (BC) in Gameweek 10 It was the usual mix of the sublime and the ridiculous from Barry.

The Toffees fell behind shortly after the half-time interval at Hill Dickinson Stadium, before a brace from Thierno Barry and a well-taken strike by Dewsbury-Hall sealed a third consecutive win in the space of eight days.

It was De Cuyper’s goal that proved the catalyst for his side’s comeback.

He had two goal involvements in 18 minutes and a hand in a third in the opening 4-0 win against Aston Villa Matty Cash spent the whole first half caught between two jobs: following De Cuyper inside or holding his line.
It’s been a whirlwind ‘out of position’ ride with De Cuyper this season, and there’s little sign of a slowdown.
De Cuyper’s not an issue for now, then, even if Luka Vuskovic (£5.2m) will likely end up being the long, long-term best pick at the back.

De Cuyper had to content himself with ‘just’ six points against the Gunners, and his sole blank so far came against the Blues.
De Cuyper is a defender in FPL but is regularly used in advanced areas.

reasons.text: Q: Is it too late to buy Maxim De Cuyper (£5.5m)? (via @vrw123 A: De Cuyper is firmly part of the current template, with just under 50% overall ownership, so you are always at risk of a rank drop if he hauls.

Then, if he later becomes a rotation risk, you can simply sell him when the fixtures toughen up, perhaps in Gameweek 18… But that might not even happen, with Kaoru Mitoma (£5.9m) perhaps not back for a while Another potential threat to De Cuyper’s place, Yankuba Minteh (£5.8m) also has an unclear fitness status, as per Neale’s early team news round-up De Cuyper is on three yellow cards.
Having provided an assist in the Red Devils’ victory over Turkey last Thursday, De Cuyper followed that up with a goal in Belgium’s riotous 4-1 win against Italy on Sunday.
It was De Cuyper’s goal that proved the catalyst for his side’s comeback.

He had two goal involvements in 18 minutes and a hand in a third in the opening 4-0 win against Aston Villa Matty Cash spent the whole first half caught between two jobs: following De Cuyper inside or holding his line.
It’s been a whirlwind ‘out of position’ ride with De Cuyper this season, and there’s little sign of a slowdown.
De Cuyper’s not an issue for now, then, even if Luka Vuskovic (£5.2m) will likely end up being the long, long-term best pick at the back.

With well-owned defenders Riccardo Calafiori (£6.0m) and Maxim De Cuyper (£5.3m) set to face tricky away fixtures at Liverpool and Manchester City in Gameweek 9, plenty of Fantasy managers will be in the market for a new defender ahead of Saturday’s deadline.

Brighton and Hove Albion duo Maxim De Cuyper (£5.3m) and Pascal Gross (£6.2m) are at the summit of FPL’s points table: But up next for the pair: two potentially tricky away days at Liverpool and Manchester City.
De Cuyper had to content himself with ‘just’ six points against the Gunners, and his sole blank so far came against the Blues.
De Cuyper is a defender in FPL but is regularly used in advanced areas.
Lewis Hall (£5.2m): A poor defence and a tough run of fixtures.

Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Wednesday 18 November 2026 11:17, UK Image: Newcastle United's Lewis Hall produces a performance for England against Spain that was years in the making The most spectacular moment came in the 18th minute.
However, Newcastle were adamant that they would not sell Hall.
Manchester United were strongly linked with a move for Hall during the summer market but were ultimately unable to get a deal over the line for the England international.

There have been suggestions that the 20-time English champions could attempt to sign Hall when the January market closes for business. © Imago Newcastle 'will refuse' to sell Hall in January However, according to The Sun , Newcastle are adamant that Hall will not be allowed to leave St James' Park when the winter window opens for business.

Three points – which lifted Everton into fifth place in the Premier League table ahead of this weekend's round of matches – were then secured against Frank Lampard's top-flight newcomers nine minutes from time when Barry slid in Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall to blast past Carl Rushworth.
